title: Ira Coffee's band in Camden and Philadelphia tap shows
summary: In Camden, Thomas joined St. Louis leader Ira Coffee's band with Norman Mason and Harry Dial, playing tap shows that tried out Philadelphia acts, including Red Skelton, then decided to go to New York.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: This is the first time you've been that far east?

Yes, my first. No, it could have been. We played a town called Jamestown, but on my own. I'm on my own now so we came to this town Camden and they had a four or five piece band. I joined a band there and we played what they called (tap) shows in those days.
JT (2 of 1) 89
Who's band was this?
This was a fellow's band by the name of Ira Coffee. He's out of St. Louis. And in that band was some good buddies, Norman Mason, and Harry Dial.
Was Harry Dial from St. Louis?

Yeah. Harry Dial was one of the first, first time I ever heard this song -- "When my sugar walks down the street, all the birds say tweet, tweet, tweet." I think he was working with Creath's band at that time, Fate Marable.

So, anyhow I come to Camden and I work for a guy, I can't remember his name. A very fine guy. We worked around, in those days was 7 days a week with a matinee and the fellow was a Scotsman, so they said. But, I don't know. They say all Scotsmen are cheap. I never thought that. Every Thursday he was there, our money was there and we played the tap shows.
A tap show is what?

These shows would go from -- see, in those days they had like Philadelphia, a blue law town. So, they'd come to Camden, it was a good rehearsal for them. They could work in Camden and still go back to Philadelphia and open on a Monday. See what I mean?
Yes.
They have a little guy out there. He's a funny guy. I saw some things I thought he was funny. I saw some things they did with the
JT (2 of 1) 90
conductor, Dr. Fiedler, with the Boston Philharmonic. Red Skelton was his name.
He was there?

Yeah. So he used to do a thing ... we never finished it. So by that (swing time ...) and how in the hell he ever found a piece from a limb, like from a tree, we'd never finish it. ... Stayed there about a year. Went on to New York.
And, this is still with Ira Coffee?
No, they were going to Atlanta. See, the show was going ... they had things where you walk around and those kind of things and people get ...
They just keep walking and walking.

They had something. The promotion promotion was terrific. I think that's what jazz needs and the band was a good band. A very good band but they were going to Atlanta and I just left St. Louis, I didn't want to go to Atlanta, you know. I had no ideas about going to Atlanta so I had a couple of dollars so I say, well, let's go to New York. I heard about these bands in New York ... so ... I go to a place called the Lenox Club and there is a fellow by the name of Sam Wooding has a band there.
